ingredients: Parboiled idli rice 100 g; white rice 100 g; split urad dal 50 g; poha about 10 g; fenugreek 1/8 tsp; salt 1/2 tsp; water as needed; oil for the griddle.
steps: 1. Rinse and soak the rice, dal and fenugreek for 4–5 hours. 2. Rinse the poha and grind it with the drained grains and enough water for a smooth batter. 3. Cover and ferment until bubbly, then stir in salt. 4. Spread a thin circle on a hot griddle, drizzle with oil and cook until golden.
serving_description: 100 g cooked plain dosai, without filling or sides

ingredients: White rice flour 200 g; instant yeast a pinch; warm water about 175 ml; coconut milk 200 ml; sugar 1 tsp; salt to taste.
steps: 1. Mix the rice flour, yeast, sugar and warm water, then cover until the batter bubbles. 2. Whisk in the coconut milk and season with salt. 3. Pour a ladle into a hot hopper pan and swirl it up the sides. 4. Cover and cook until the rim crisps and the center sets.

ingredients: White rice 60 g; split urad dal 20 g; water as needed; salt to taste.
steps: 1. Soak the rice and dal separately until softened. 2. Grind the dal until fluffy and the rice to a slightly grainy batter. 3. Combine with salt and ferment until risen. 4. Spoon into idli moulds and steam for about 12 to 15 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. 5. Let the idlis rest briefly before removing them from the moulds.
source: Nutrition Indian Nutrient Databank ASC144 https://github.com/lindsayjaacks/Indian-Nutrient-Databank-INDB- via https://idyora.com/calories/idli and https://nnwa.in/foods/dishes/idli/ | Rounded portion values normalized to the 25 g reference piece; total carbohydrate includes fiber. Technique reference https://www.vegrecipesofindia.com/idli-recipe-how-to-make-soft-idlis/

ingredients: Cooked layered roti 454 g; prepared Sri Lankan chicken curry with gravy 400 g; eggs 150 g (about 3); oil 27 g; carrots 75 g; onion 55 g; cabbage 100 g; leeks 90 g; garlic 9 g; ginger 6 g; green chilies 15 g.
steps: 1. Slice the cooked roti into narrow strips and shred the cooked chicken. 2. Fry the onion, garlic, ginger and chilies in oil, then stir-fry the vegetables. 3. Push the vegetables aside, scramble the eggs in the pan and mix them through. 4. Add the roti, shredded chicken and curry gravy. Toss over high heat until hot throughout.
source: Recipe adapted from The Flavor Bender https://www.theflavorbender.com/sri-lankan-chicken-kottu-roti-koththu/ using local green chilies and prepared chicken curry; USDA ARS SR28 ingredient profiles https://www.ars.usda.gov/northeast-area/beltsville-md-bhnrc/beltsville-human-nutrition-research-center/methods-and-application-of-food-composition-laboratory/mafcl-site-pages/sr28-page-reports/ for egg, canola oil and vegetables; Parata row used as roti proxy; chicken curry from Table 2 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfca.2025.107230 (digestible carbohydrate plus fiber). Ingredient totals divided by assumed 1250 g cooked yield. Chicken is the reference variant. Match to training photos remains unverified.

ingredients: White short-grain rice 2 cups; water 3 3/4 cups; coconut milk 400 ml; salt 2 tsp.
steps: 1. Rinse the rice, then simmer it in water until very soft. 2. Stir in the salted coconut milk and cook gently until the mixture thickens and holds together. 3. Press it into an even slab while warm, let it set and cut into diamonds.

ingredients: All-purpose white wheat flour about 250 g; water as needed; salt to taste; about 15 g oil retained from kneading, shaping and griddle cooking.
steps: 1. Knead the flour, salt, water and a little oil into a soft dough. 2. Divide into eight balls, coat lightly with oil and rest covered until the dough stretches easily. 3. Stretch each ball into a thin sheet, fold into layers and flatten lightly. 4. Griddle both sides until golden and gently press the sides to loosen the layers.

ingredients: Roasted white rice flour 300 g; fresh grated coconut 150 g; salt 1 tsp; warm water about 200 ml.
steps: 1. Rub the rice flour, most of the coconut and the salt together. 2. Sprinkle in water gradually and rub until small, loose crumbs form. 3. Layer the crumbs and reserved coconut loosely in a pittu tube. 4. Steam until the flour is cooked through and release the cylinder.

ingredients: White Nadu rice 1 cup; water about 1 1/2 cups for absorption cooking, adjusted for the rice and pot.
steps: 1. Rinse the rice and drain it well. 2. Add fresh water and bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender. 3. Rest covered off the heat for 10 minutes and fluff.

ingredients: Roasted white rice flour 350 g; salt 6 g; hot water up to 400 ml; oil 1 tsp for the mats.
steps: 1. Stir hot water into the salted flour a little at a time to form a soft dough. 2. Fill a string-hopper press and squeeze thin coils onto lightly oiled mats. 3. Steam covered over boiling water until the strands are set and lift away cleanly. Check around 5 minutes and allow longer for thicker nests.
